title: Flight Control Weekly — Shift Handoff and Degradation Playbook
content:
Flight Control Weekly — Shift Handoff + Degradation Playbook

Date: 2026-03-10
Facilitator: Jordan Patel
Duration: 45m (standup format)
Attendees: Jordan Patel, Sofia Chen, Diego Morales, Priya Singh, Lena Hoffman, Ashok Varma (observability)
Absentees: N/A
Recorded in channel: #release-flight-control

Purpose
- Sync on upcoming rollouts, surface risks for the next 72 hours, and confirm handoff owners for the on-call shift window.
- Validate and iterate on the lightweight degradation playbook for degradation-mode routing and capacity shedding.

Quick snapshot (metrics at 10:00 PT)
- Median p99 latency (text generation): 210ms (hosted-prod-us-west)
- Token/sec throughput per GPU pool: 18k
- Error rate (5m rolling): 0.14% (ingress retries)
- Cache hit ratio (prefix KV): 52%
- Active canaries: candidate-model-v2 (3%) on pool-dedicated-east

Agenda items + notes
1) Canary progress for candidate-model-v2
- Diego: Canary steady for 18 hours, small increase in prompt-review latency (+40ms). Quality team flagged two regressions on long-context prompts (JIRA RI-4128).
- Decision: Pause expansion beyond 3% until PR for attention-kernel fallback lands. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-03-12 EOD.
- Action: Attach failing prompt set and golden-output to RI-4128. Owner: Priya.

2) Degradation playbook v0.3 walkthrough
- Key idea: graceful degradation prioritized by customer tier and route importance.
- Steps summarized:
  a) Detect: sustained p99 > 600ms OR token backlog > 45k for 10m -> trigger "degradation-check" alert.
  b) Assess: SRE on call runs quick triage, checks cache-hit/disk-swap and routing logs.
  c) Mitigate: sequentially apply controls - enable KV-prefix-only caching, reduce max tokens per request to 1024 for non-enterprise routes, disable low-tier batch-warming.
  d) Fallback: reroute non-critical traffic to compatible smaller model family (model-sm-quant) with documented SSE differences.
  e) Restore: reverse mitigations after metrics normalize for 20m.
- Concern: need automated rollout for token-limit enforcement. Ticket created: RI-4152. Owner: Jordan.

3) Shift handoff checklist refinement
- Current pain: long checklists cause handoffs to skip items under busy conditions. Proposed condensed checklist (3 priority checks):
  1) Verify canaries are within expected latency delta and error budget.
  2) Confirm autoscaler target headroom >= 20% for each pool.
  3) Look at trace-sample for top 3 routes for any fresh regressions.
- Implementation: build 3 quick indicators in console topbar. Prototype ticket: RI-4161. Owner: Lena.

4) Hotfix staging window and risk lane coordination
- Upcoming non-blocking hotfix deploy: 2026-03-13 08:00 PT -> incremental kernel tweak (optimized matmul kernel) to reduce p50 by ~5%.
- Risk: binary mismatch with older quantized kernels could increase memory use on older nodes. Mitigation: restrict rollout to nodes with kernel tag "matmul-2026q1" and preflight memory smoke test.
- Action: Release engineer to run dry-run on staging cluster (RI-4169). Owner: Sofia.

5) Observability gaps and temporary probes
- Ashok: need a short-term probe to detect token cache thrashing (spike in eviction rate). Plan: add eviction-rate metric and alert threshold > 200 evictions/min. Low-effort instrumentation to be merged today. Owner: Ashok.

Decision log (what we agreed)
- Hold canary expansion for candidate-model-v2 until regressions fixed (see RI-4128).
- Adopt condensed handoff checklist and ship console indicator MVP by end of sprint.
- Approve hotfix staging window with strict node-tag gating and preflight smoke tests.

Action items (owner, due date, note)
- RI-4128: Attach failing prompts + golden outputs (Priya Singh) — due 2026-03-11.
- RI-4152: Implement token-limit enforcement feature toggle (Jordan Patel) — due 2026-03-18.
- RI-4161: Console topbar indicator prototype + mock (Lena Hoffman) — due 2026-03-15.
- RI-4169: Staging dry-run for matmul kernel tweak (Sofia Chen) — due 2026-03-12 before 18:00 PT.
- RI-4175: Add eviction-rate probe and alert (Ashok Varma) — due 2026-03-10 (in progress).

Risk register (brief)
- RISK-01: Canary expansion could surface quality regressions impacting high-traffic routes. Likelihood: medium, Impact: high. Mitigation: pause expansion and require golden prompt pass.
- RISK-02: Kernel hotfix memory mismatch on legacy nodes. Likelihood: low, Impact: medium. Mitigation: node-tag gating + smoke test.
- RISK-03: Lack of quick handoff indicators increases mean-time-to-detect during shift changes. Likelihood: medium, Impact: medium. Mitigation: build console topbar indicators.

Notes, follow-ups and open questions
- Consider running a weekly "flight-control dry run" where we simulate a degradation scenario during low traffic to exercise playbook steps end-to-end. Proposal: schedule 2026-03-19 02:00 PT. Owner: Jordan.
- Should we centralize canary outputs in an S3 folder per model version for easy audit? Follow-up with legal for retention policy. Owner: Diego.
- How do we communicate degraded-mode behavior to customers? Product to draft messaging templates for non-enterprise customers. Owner: Priya (sync with product-hosted-api).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call handoff (condensed)
- Confirm canary stable (latency delta < 20% and errors < 0.5%).
- Autoscaler headroom >= 20% per pool.
- No elevated eviction-rate alerts in last 30m.
- Note active rollouts and responsible release owner.

Next meeting
- Regular cadence: weekly, Tuesdays 09:00 PT. Next scheduled: 2026-03-17.

Artifacts & references
